Done implementing. Nothing was run or tested, as requested — these are code + design only.

## What I built

A resumable, three-stage pipeline (generate → judge → analyze) replicating **Section 2** of the paper, scoped to `gemma-3-27b-it`, `gemma-3-12b-it`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`.

```
config.yaml                 all knobs (models, sampling preset, judge, seed)
.env.example                API keys
requirements.txt
scripts/run_elicitation.py  generate + judge (resumable phases)
scripts/analyze.py          metrics + optional inter-rater agreement
distress_eval/              prompts, conditions, wildchat, clients, judge,
                            conversation, runner, analysis, storage, config
DESIGN.md                   every decision + deviations + gaps (the main read)
README.md                   quickstart + outputs
```

## The decisions worth flagging now (all detailed in DESIGN.md)

1. **The judge model in the paper is retired.** The paper judges with `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, whose snapshot hit end-of-life on **2026-06-15** — 10 days before today, so it 404s. I defaulted the judge to `claude-sonnet-4-6` (configurable back), kept the Appendix B.2 prompt **verbatim**, and wired up the paper's GPT-5-mini agreement check so you can quantify any judge drift. This is the biggest threat to exact numeric reproduction and I called it out prominently.

2. **What "a response" means.** The paper's "4000 responses/model" is ambiguous (conversation vs turn). The WildChat "20 prompts × 40 samples = 800" pins it down: **a response = a conversation**, and I score its **final** turn for the headline — which reproduces every per-category total exactly (2000/400/600/200/800). But I store *all* turns, so the per-turn Figure 3 view and alternative aggregations (max-over-turns, pooled) are recomputable without regenerating.

3. **8 conditions / 5 categories** reconciled the only way that sums to 8: numeric is one condition mixing both puzzles; triggers=2, tones=3, extended + wildchat. 

4. **Gemma defaults to local vLLM** (faithful to the paper, avoids API-side sampling/safety confounds), one-line switchable to OpenRouter if you have no GPU. Gemini via OpenRouter with thinking disabled.

5. **Filled gaps**, each documented: `max_tokens=2048` (paper unspecified — matters because breakdowns are long), judge temperature 0, rejection-phrase pools assembled from the quoted examples, WildChat filtered only by length, normal-approx 95% CIs.

DESIGN.md §13 has the full deviation table and §14 lists the five questions I'd put to the authors. I deliberately left out Sections 3–4 (base/instruct, DPO) and the non-Gemma/Gemini baselines per your scope — though adding baselines back is just more entries under `models:`.

A good next step when you're ready: run `sampling.preset: smoke` end-to-end to validate wiring before the full 4000-conversation preset (which is ~56k judge calls across the four models).
